clue.text: Small volume about Scottish girl (not English), a standard work

indicators.note: about means one piece is placed around the other, so the volume goes round the girl

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, is a small measure of volume

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for English from the girl

parts.note: a lassie is a Scots word for a girl

explanation.surface: A slim book about a Scottish lass, written without English, has become a standard text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not English' removes the E from the girl, and 'about' puts what is left inside the small volume. 'Scottish girl' is the clue's way of asking for the Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work regarded as a model or standard of its kind.

clue.text: It's six-sided, or eight

definitions.meaning: a solid with six square faces
two multiplied by itself three times gives eight, the third power of two

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is arithmetic: eight is the third power of two.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular solid has six square faces, and eight is two raised to the third power.

clue.text: Demo loses leader and chief

indicators.note: losing its leader means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: A protest without its organiser, and its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: MARCH drops its first letter M ('loses leader').
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective arch means principal or chief, as in archenemy.

clue.text: Shore base, possibly with winding road

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of base could be arranged another way
a winding road twists, so its letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A coastal base, perhaps reached by a twisting road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' makes SEAB from BASE and 'winding' makes OARD from ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaboard is the coastline or shore region of a country.

clue.text: Thick ground cover, good going for cricket, initially?

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of cricket is used
good going means the letter for good departs from the grass

parts.note: grass covers the ground

explanation.surface: A dense cover of grass makes good going for a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'going' the G for good leaves GRASS, and 'for cricket, initially' sets the C of cricket in its place at the front, giving RASS after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means stupid or insensitive, a sense close to thick meaning dim-witted.

clue.text: Spasmodic? Well, not totally occupied

parts.note: well in the sense of healthy means fit

indicators.note: not totally means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: occupied, like a full room, means full

explanation.surface: Asked whether something was spasmodic, the reply is that it was only partly occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: FULL loses its last letter ('not totally') to give FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitful means irregular, happening in bursts, which is what spasmodic describes.

clue.text: One stupid person at party turned up as a crustacean

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a sop is a feeble, soft-headed person

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A foolish person turned up at a party dressed as a crustacean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses DO to OD.
explanation.definitionFit: An isopod is a crustacean such as the woodlouse, with seven pairs of similar legs.

clue.text: Young horse, say, with horse-breaker to produce delaying action

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a young horse is used for its sound

parts.note: a filly is a young female horse
a buster, as in bronco-buster, breaks in wild horses

explanation.surface: A young horse and a horse-breaker are used to produce a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: FILI is how the start of the answer sounds, like FILLY ('say'). BUSTER is American slang for a horse-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A filibuster is a long speech used to delay or block a vote, a delaying tactic.

clue.text: Portable recording device used by a photographer

parts.note: light things are easily carried
a meter is an instrument that records a measurement

explanation.surface: A handheld recording gadget that a photographer carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer uses this instrument to measure the brightness of light for exposure.

clue.text: Punter, we hear, at this card game

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for a punter is used for its sound

parts.note: a backer is someone who places a bet

explanation.surface: A gambler is spotted at this card game, we're told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' works on the punter's word: said aloud it matches the start of the game's name, and the clue's own 'at' finishes it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game on which players bet.

clue.text: A sharp bend, of course

definitions.meaning: an abrupt angle in a road or path
on a golf course, a hole whose fairway bends sharply

explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' is a golf course, not the phrase meaning naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogleg is a sharp angle, especially a golf hole bending left or right.

clue.text: Tentative proposal of charge on line about to arise

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: in a down clue arising means reading upwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A tentative proposal of a fee on the line is about to come up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arise' reverses RE to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeler is a cautious approach made to test opinion before a firm offer.

clue.text: Trashed combo upset, wounded

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trashed band set-up leaves everyone upset and hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means out of action through injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Hors de combat is French for out of the fight, applied to someone disabled by wounds.

clue.text: Musical instrument whose parts only differ at the top

definitions.text: Musical instrument whose parts only differ at the top

parts.words: Musical instrument whose parts only differ at the top
parts.note: an instrument whose name has two halves that rhyme, matching except for their opening letters

explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'the top' is the start of each half of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cranked stringed folk instrument whose name is two rhyming halves.

clue.text: I (scorer) end with wrong result, to may need to do this

indicators.note: with a wrong result the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A scorer who ends with a wrong result may need to think again.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'to' reads like a slip for 'so'; the anagram of I, SCORER and END under 'wrong' stands complete.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider is to think again about a decision, as a scorer with a wrong total would.

clue.text: Make call in a French railway, not making a mistake

parts.note: une is French for a

indicators.note: in means the call goes inside the railway abbreviation

parts.note: to ring is to make a telephone call

explanation.surface: Making a phone call on a French railway, without making an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a French' is the French indefinite article, a common crossword device; 'in' puts the call inside the railway abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Unerringly means without error, unfailingly accurately.

clue.text: A perfect beginner?

parts.note: someone perfect has ..., and a beginner is a learner or trainee

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words to see why a perfect person fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is someone new to an activity, a learner or beginner.

clue.text: Look where to find a cathedral

definitions.meaning: a bishop's diocese, whose seat is a cathedral

explanation.definitionFit: To see is to look, and a see is a bishop's diocese centred on a cathedral.

clue.text: I could have been in rough water but I'm still all in one piece

definitions.text: I could have been in rough water but I'm still all in one piece

parts.words: I could have been in rough water but I'm still all in one piece
parts.note: a garment worn in the sea that is a single piece of clothing rather than a damaged survivor

explanation.walkthrough: 'in one piece' suggests surviving unharmed but means a one-piece garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimsuit is a garment for swimming, often a one-piece.

clue.text: Associated pair in the clouds making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the letters read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the word clouds

explanation.surface: A partnership up in the clouds makes a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes OUD from cl-OUD-s and 'making a comeback' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair of people associated in performing or working together.

clue.text: Something mislaid? Look here!

parts.note: the place to search for a lost item reads as advice to search in all places

explanation.walkthrough: 'Look here!' sounds like pointing to one spot, but the answer is the opposite advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Everywhere means in all places, which is where you look for something lost.

clue.text: Provided uplifts at the time of company's collapse

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means raising, reading the word upwards

parts.note: if means provided that
as means while, at the time of
co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Funding provided lifts the company at the time of its collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifts' reverses IF to FI.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating failure, a complete collapse.

clue.text: For news of a pillar of the establishment?

definitions.text: For news of a pillar of the establishment?

parts.words: For news of a pillar of the establishment?
parts.note: a pillar can be a newspaper feature and chatter is news of public figures

explanation.walkthrough: 'pillar' suggests a respected person but means a newspaper feature.
explanation.definitionFit: This newspaper feature reports rumour and news about prominent people.

clue.text: Start off without a meal

indicators.note: without tells us the letter a is taken out

parts.note: to launch is to start something off

explanation.surface: A day started off without breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A from LAUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is the midday meal.

clue.text: Opening that could be barred

parts.note: an entrance closed with bars, or simply a hinged barrier made of bars

explanation.definitionFit: A gate is an opening in a wall or fence, often made of bars.

clue.text: Officer supports exercises at a rapid pace

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means sitting underneath, so the officer comes below

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer backs exercises done at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts LT under PE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelt is a fast speed, as in running at full pelt.

clue.text: This plant is hard, brittle

indicators.note: brittle things break up, so these letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: This plant is tough yet fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brittle' rearranges IS HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a plant grown for its peppery root.

clue.text: Most of the piece about new island is to develop slowly

indicators.note: about means the shortened piece goes around the rest
most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: an item is a piece
Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: Most of the article about a new island is developed slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: ITEM loses its last letter ('Most of') to give ITE, which goes 'about' N and CUBA.
explanation.definitionFit: To incubate is to develop gradually, as eggs or an idea do over time.

clue.text: Unknown quantity as missile plant

parts.note: y is a variable in algebra, an unknown quantity
an arrow is a missile shot from a bow

explanation.surface: An unknown quantity used as a missile plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a flowering plant, also called milfoil.

clue.text: Unenviable position of those with a time in conflict?

indicators.note: in conflict means at odds, so the letters fight their way into new order

explanation.surface: An unenviable position for people with time against them in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conflict' rearranges THOSE, A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the hot seat means being in a difficult position under pressure.
